newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Feb 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Feb 4.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on February 4. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
President Suharto says the government's decision to increase the price of fertilizer and unhulled rice is fixed.
The government has restricted major gatherings by political and social organisations in the run up to the May general election, calling on local administrators to issue permits sparingly.

Indonesia has warned the European Union it would not discuss what it considers "extraneous issues" such as East Timor in next week's meeting between ministers of the EU and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN).

A private company set up to finance Indonesia's first passenger jet project is to split 400,000 of its two million shares, each with a nominal value of $1,000 (2.36 million rupiah) into smaller shares with a 5,000 rupiah par value. The move will allow average people to buy shares in the N-2130 project.
General Hartono, chief of staff of the army, has warned that the armed forces will not hesitate to take repressive actions if riots break out again.
Indonesia will reduce its coffee exports by 150,000 60-kg bags in the first half of this year under a plan adopted by key producers in Brazil, a coffee industry executive said.
